sections.category: Unsloth ships v0.1.47-beta with GLM-5.2 support, a redesigned Model Hub, and an auto-fit algorithm that triples usable context length on a single GPU

bullets.body: The Unsloth fine-tuning stack tagged a fresh build, v0.1.47-beta ("GLM 5.2 + Model Hub + 3x longer contexts"), on June 18. The headline training-time change is a new auto-fit context algorithm coupled with multi-token prediction that the project reports roughly triples the usable context length that fits in fixed memory: on a single 32GB GPU in f16 the maximum context expands from about 23,040 to 64,000 tokens without spilling, which directly lowers the hardware bar for long-context fine-tuning runs on consumer and single-card setups. The release adds full support for Zhipu's GLM-5.2 across all of its reasoning levels (high / max / disabled thinking modes) inside Unsloth Studio, and pairs it with a full-page Model Hub redesign carrying a trending feed, search and persisted state, README previews in split view, and faster downloads over Xet transport with automatic HTTP fallback. Supporting changes include a new --secure Cloudflare-only mode for end-to-end-encrypted studios, restored vLLM 0.22+ compatibility with automatic multi-token-prediction fallback under tensor parallelism, DeepSeek-OCR vision support, better Blackwell-GPU handling, and a modularization that lets export, chat, training and recipes run independently without contending for the same resources. As a beta the numbers are the project's own, but the context-fit gain is the kind of concrete training-side state-change that matters for local fine-tuning economics rather than a benchmark headline. sections.category: Liquid AI releases a pair of 350M open-weight retrieval models built for fast on-device multilingual search across 11 languages

bullets.body: Liquid AI published two small open-weight retrieval models on June 19 under its LFM Open License v1.0: LFM2.5-Embedding-350M, a dense bi-encoder that maps a document to a single vector, and LFM2.5-ColBERT-350M, a late-interaction model that produces per-token vectors for finer word-by-word matching. Both are at 350 million parameters and are derived from a shared backbone by swapping causal attention for bidirectional attention ("bidirectional patches") so the encoder can attend to full context, and both cover 11 languages (Arabic, German, English, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Swedish). The pitch is class-leading retrieval quality at a size that runs on a laptop CPU: the ColBERT variant is reported at 0.605 NDCG@10 on NanoBEIR and 0.694 Recall@20 on the multilingual MKQA-11 set, claimed to beat larger competitors, and the GGUF builds run under llama.cpp with median query latency below 10 ms on a MacBook Pro M4 Max. Retrieval/embedding models are the unglamorous backbone of practical RAG, and a permissively licensed 350M pair that is genuinely fast on commodity edge hardware is exactly the kind of on-device-inference component that lets local LLM stacks do grounded search without a server-side embedding call. As with any single-vendor launch the headline numbers are self-reported and await third-party reproduction. sections.category: Coding-agent harnesses ship control and recording features in the same window: Nous Hermes adds a minimal Blank Slate mode, OpenAI's Codex learns tasks by watching once, and Cisco open-sources a Claude-Code-driven prompt optimizer

bullets.body: Three concrete state-changes landed across the agent-harness / coding-agent space on June 18-20. Nous Research added a Blank Slate setup mode to its open-source Hermes Agent framework (June 20): instead of booting with the full feature surface enabled, an agent starts with only a provider/model, a File Operations toolset and a Terminal toolset, while web access, browser, code execution, vision, memory, delegation, cron, skills, plugins and MCP servers all stay off until explicitly turned on. The choice is written durably to disk via platform_toolsets.cli (enabled set) and agent.disabled_toolsets (explicit off list) so disabled capabilities will not silently re-enable after a hermes update; the move is squarely a least-privilege / attack-surface-reduction posture for autonomous agents. The same day OpenAI shipped Record & Replay for its Codex macOS app (build 26.616): a user walks the agent through a multi-step desktop workflow once and it is captured as a reusable "skill" Codex can re-run unattended (Computer Use required; not available in the EU/UK/Switzerland yet). And Cisco open-sourced FAPO (June 20), a Claude-Code-driven prompt optimizer that evaluates whole multi-step LLM pipelines rather than isolated prompts, attributes failures to a specific stage (retrieval, cascading empty-output, format-masking, or reasoning), and escalates from prompt edits to parameter tweaks to structural chain rewrites; an agentic loop proposes variants while an independent agent validates them, with the team reporting a +14.1-point mean gain over GEPA across 15 of 18 model-benchmark pairs. sections.category: NVIDIA's training-free SpatialClaw agent treats a live Python kernel as the action interface and posts the top score across 20 spatial-reasoning benchmarks

bullets.body: NVIDIA researchers released SpatialClaw on June 19, a training-free framework that gives vision-language models a way to reason about object localization and 3D relationships they normally struggle with, without any model-specific or benchmark-specific tuning. Instead of retraining, SpatialClaw wraps a stateful Python kernel that is pre-loaded with the input frames and a set of perception primitives, and the agent writes one Python cell per step into that persistent kernel, composing and revising perception-tool calls as it goes; because the kernel is live, the agent can do genuine test-time computation, for example switching from a centroid-distance heuristic to a KD-tree nearest-neighbor search mid-task rather than committing to a fixed plan up front. The reported results put code-as-action ahead of prior tool-use approaches: 59.9% average accuracy across 20 spatial benchmarks, +11.2 points over the SpaceTools baseline, with the largest gains on dynamic tasks (DSI-Bench +17.6, MindCube +15.3) and consistency across six backbones spanning 26B to 397B parameters. The work is open: code is on GitHub (NVlabs/SpatialClaw) with a project page and paper PDF, which makes it a reproducible applied-research result rather than a vendor benchmark claim, and it strengthens the broader "let the agent emit executable code as its action space" pattern now showing up in spatial and agentic reasoning. sections.category: AI events to plan around now: the confidential-computing and offensive-security tracks are days out, then the AI Engineer World's Fair, with the chip and security calendar running into the fall

bullets.body: The forward calendar across all three sub-tracks, with the soonest events now only days away and nothing yet past its end date. Mainstream dev/data: Snowflake runs a virtual Dev Day on June 25 (two luminary talks plus a hands-on agentic-AI lab); the AI Engineer World's Fair takes over Moscone West with main programming June 29 through July 2 (an optional New Engineer Orientation on June 28), billed as the largest technical AI-engineering conference with over 20 tracks, around 250 speakers, dedicated Inference and Security tracks, and OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Amazon AGI Labs and Microsoft on the floor, preceded by the official AIE World's Fair Hackathon with Cerebral Valley on June 27-28; further out, GitHub Universe returns October 28-29 and AWS re:Invent runs November 30 through December 4 in Las Vegas. AI-security: the Confidential Computing Summit lands June 23-24 at the San Francisco Mint (Linux Foundation and OPAQUE, with confidential-AI and data-sovereignty keynotes featuring AMD, Google, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Meta, Samsung and others); AI Tinkerers San Francisco hosts an Offensive Security Demo Night on June 25 with live autonomous-pentesting-agent demos (sponsor XBOW); SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit follows August 11-12 at Half Moon Bay; Black Hat USA's AI Summit runs August 1-6 in Las Vegas alongside DEF CON's AI Village; and OWASP Global AppSec USA is November 5-6 in San Francisco. Zenity's AI Agent Security Summit series remains on the watch list. AI-chip/hardware: AMD's Advancing AI 2026 is set for July 23 at Moscone (Instinct MI400-series focus expected); Hot Chips 2026 runs August 23-25 at Stanford; and the AI Infra Summit is September 15-17 at the Santa Clara Convention Center.
